brief.subject: Diesel jumps 7.6 cents; LA-Long Beach rail backlog builds
brief.headline: Diesel Up 7.6 Cents to $6.352 as Executives Warn of High Prices Into 2027
brief.dek: Diesel climbs again, a port rail backlog grows in Southern California, and FMCSA purges thousands of driver training providers.
brief.lede: The national diesel average rose 7.6 cents last week to $6.352 per gallon, and fuel executives say tight refining capacity could keep prices high into spring 2027.

sections.heading: Diesel Climbs Again
bullets: $6.352 per gallon: the EIA national diesel average for the week of 2026-10-26, eating further into per-mile margins.
Up 7.6 cents (1.2%) week over week, so check that fuel surcharges on your contracts keep pace.
Down 3.0 cents over four weeks, meaning last week's jump erased most of the recent relief.
Fuel and truck stop executives warn limited refining and pipeline capacity could keep diesel elevated into spring 2027.

sections.heading: Port Freight Piling Up
bullets: Nearly 35,700 import containers are waiting on on-dock trains at Los Angeles and Long Beach amid reported railcar shortages.
Record volumes plus slow rail could push more inland moves onto trucks, opening drayage and transload opportunities.
Port Houston container volumes rose 11% in September on surging imports, a Gulf Coast lane worth watching.

sections.heading: FMCSA Purges Training Providers
bullets: More than 10,000 driver training providers have been removed from FMCSA's registry since December 2025.
Fleets hiring new CDL holders should confirm a candidate's training provider is still listed.

sections.heading: Big Carriers Report Mixed Q3
bullets: Landstar saw strong dry van and flatbed demand from tight capacity and data center buildouts, though insurance claims hurt results.
Werner expects cost headwinds to linger into the first quarter while it works back to mid-cycle margins.
RXO founder Brad Jacobs backed C.H. Robinson's acquisition of RXO, citing the need for scale in brokerage.

sections.heading: Cross-Border and Policy Watch
bullets: Mexican trucking groups agreed to four negotiating sessions with officials after a strike disrupted highways in 19 states.
USTR's pause on China-linked vessel fees is set to lift Nov. 9, but an extension to January is under consideration.
USPS plans a weekly fuel surcharge in 2027 tied to diesel and jet fuel, matching FedEx and UPS.
